doc.title: Harry "Sweets" Edison interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, September 3, 1995

title: Recognizable trumpet styles and the Basie band's style
summary: Shavers, Dizzy, Armstrong and Red Allen each had distinct sounds, as did Teddy Wilson and the Basie band.

story.theme_name: Remembering the early trumpeters and their styles
story.community_name: Bix Beiderbecke: hearing, copying and remembering him

blocks.x: had their own style. They had their own sound. There was no doubt when you heard them playing you could be ten miles away and hear them play and say, “that’s Charlie Shavers—that’s Dizzy—that’s Louis Armstrong—that’s Red Allen.” Bunny Berigan had a good sound of his own. But Teddy Wilson, he had a style which was simple but beautiful, you know?
And the Basie band itself had a style.
